summary: Under high CPU contention, the Ruby SDK can emit un-replayable workflow history due to inconsistent command flushing, where activity starts get split into unexpected partial batches. This permanently breaks workflows and requires manual reset/termination to resolve.
userImpact: Workflows become permanently broken and unreplayable under CPU contention, requiring manual intervention to reset or terminate them.
rootCause: Sync primitives cause inconsistent command flushing under CPU contention, splitting activity start commands into unexpected partial batches across workflow tasks. This violates determinism during replay on new workers.
proposedFix: A proposed fix exists on a fork/branch but requires validation as it was AI-generated.
keyQuote: When the SDK is operating under high cpu contention it is possible to emit un-replayable workflow history permanently breaking a workflow
